overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: The RAG obtains 1 of 3 mechanism-first true positives at high_and_moderate and 2 of 3 when low confidence is included; the queue-triage and beacon mechanisms are fully captured, while the suppression-rule finding is only partial.

main_failure_modes: All three findings use near-neighbor taxonomy labels instead of the hidden target labels, producing strict false positives and false negatives.
The suppression-rule finding describes automation complacency but does not fully identify the hidden illusion-of-control mechanism.
The queue-triage finding is low confidence, so it is missed at the recommended high_and_moderate threshold.
main_strengths: All three identified findings are localized to the correct positive decision-point segments.
The queue-triage and beacon findings state mechanisms that fully match their hidden instances under the mechanism-first scorecard.
Interview quotations are valid, accurately attributed, and tied to the participant's actual reasoning rather than interviewer prompts or hindsight alone.
The negative escalation segment is correctly left undetected, with no false alarms.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong segment localization and meaningful mechanism recovery but poor strict taxonomy alignment. The gap between strict and mechanism-first scores is therefore diagnostic of label selection rather than failure to find the relevant reasoning episodes.
